what_its_for: This medicine is a nutrition solution given directly into your vein (IV). It contains building blocks called amino acids, which your body uses to make proteins. It is used when you cannot eat enough food by mouth or through a feeding tube, such as after surgery, during serious illness, or when your digestive system is not working properly. It helps your body heal, maintain muscle, and stay strong.
how_to_take: This medicine is given to you by a trained nurse or doctor through an IV (intravenous) line, usually into a large vein in your chest, neck, or arm. You will never give this to yourself by mouth — it is only for use in a vein. If you are receiving this at home through a home infusion service, a trained nurse will show you exactly how to set up and manage your IV line. Never change the drip rate or mix in other medicines unless your doctor or pharmacist tells you to do so.
dosing: Your doctor will decide exactly how much you need based on your weight, health condition, lab results, and nutritional needs. Doses are highly individualized. A typical adult may receive anywhere from 1 to 2 grams of amino acids per kilogram of body weight per day, but your actual dose may be different. The solution is usually given slowly and continuously over many hours or an entire day. Your care team will monitor you closely and adjust your dose as needed.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given by a healthcare professional in a hospital or through a scheduled home infusion service, missed doses are managed by your care team. If your IV infusion stops unexpectedly, is interrupted, or you notice it is not running as scheduled, contact your nurse, doctor, or home infusion pharmacy right away. Do not try to speed up the drip to make up for a missed or slow infusion — this can be dangerous.
storage: This solution should be stored in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight, ideally between 36°F and 77°F (2°C and 25°C). Do not freeze the solution. If it has been frozen, do not use it. Before use, check the bag or bottle carefully — do not use it if you see particles floating in the solution, if the solution looks cloudy or discolored, or if the bag or seal is damaged. Once opened or connected to your IV line, use it within the time frame your pharmacist or nurse instructs, typically within 24 hours. Keep it and all medicines out of the reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating or drinking anything that your doctor has restricted while on this therapy. Do not add any other medicines, vitamins, or supplements to the IV bag unless your doctor or pharmacist has specifically approved and instructed you to do so — mixing unknown substances can cause dangerous reactions. Avoid touching the IV connection points with unclean hands to reduce infection risk. Do not adjust the IV flow rate on your own. Avoid alcohol unless your doctor says it is safe. Limit activities that could dislodge your IV line, such as heavy lifting or rough movement around the IV site.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor, nurse, or home infusion pharmacy right away if you notice any of the following: fever, chills, or sweating; redness, swelling, pain, or drainage at your IV site; shortness of breath or difficulty breathing; swelling in your legs, feet, or hands; sudden confusion or unusual tiredness; nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain; high or low blood sugar symptoms such as shakiness, excessive thirst, or frequent urination; yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); or if the IV solution looks unusual, the bag leaks, or the infusion pump alarms. Seek emergency help (call 911) if you have chest pain, severe difficulty breathing, or signs of a severe allergic reaction such as hives, throat tightening, or rapid heartbeat.
when_it_works: This medicine starts working as soon as it enters your bloodstream. However, you may not feel an immediate difference. Over several days to weeks of therapy, your body should begin to heal more effectively, maintain or rebuild muscle, improve wound healing, and support your immune system. Your doctor will check your blood work regularly — such as blood sugar, kidney function, liver function, and electrolytes — to make sure the treatment is working and to adjust it as needed.
special_populations: Older adults: May need lower doses and closer monitoring for kidney and liver function, as well as fluid balance. Children and infants: Dosing is very different for children and must be carefully calculated by a specialist. Amino acid solutions specifically designed for pediatric patients are usually preferred. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: This therapy can be used if medically necessary, but your doctor will closely monitor both you and your baby. People with kidney disease: Amino acid doses may need to be reduced to avoid putting extra strain on the kidneys. Special kidney-formulated amino acid solutions may be used instead. People with liver disease: Liver disease can affect how your body handles amino acids. Your doctor will monitor your liver closely and may use a specially formulated solution. People with diabetes: This solution can affect blood sugar levels. Your blood sugar will be monitored frequently, and insulin may be needed.
